blocks.text: Participles are "verbal adjectives". The long form of the past passive participle denotes the (direct) object of someone's action.

The active participle is also a long form adjective, but it always denotes the performer of the action: *пишущий студент* = **студент**, **который пишет** (who writes); *писавший студент* = **студент**, **который писал** (who was writing).

points: Present active participles formed from the present tense of imperfective verbs.

Past active participles formed from the past tenses of both imperfective and perfective verbs. No participles are formed from future tenses. All active participles are used only as modifiers; they have no short forms.

Present active participles are formed from the 3rd person plural of the present tense by replacing the last **-т** of the verb by **-щ** plus adjectival ending: (**они**) **работают** — **работающий**, **работающая**, **работающее**, **работающие**; (**они**) **говорят** — **говорящий**, **говорящая**, **говорящее**, **говорящие**.
From **-ся** verbs the particle **-ся** (never **-сь!**) is added to the ending: **моются** — **моющийся**, **моющаяся**, **моющееся**, **моющиеся**.

In almost all present active participles the stress is the same as in the 3rd person plural, with the exception of **мочь** — **могущий** and a group of 2nd-conjugation verbs in which the stress coincides with the infinitive: **курящий**, **носящий**, **смотрящий**, **находящийся**.

blocks.text: Present active participles are declined like adjectives and always agree in gender, number and case with the word modified: *Я вижу сидящую девушку. Мы говорим с отъезжающими офицерами.* If used singly, the participle always precedes the modified word: *спящий человек; горящее здание.* A participial phrase may be placed before or after the modified word. In the «**который**» clauses which replace present active participial phrases, «**который**» will always be the subject of the clause (in the nominative case), the verb being in the present tense:

items: Сюда придут студенты, кончающие школу через месяц. = …которые кончают школу через месяц.
Дайте это студентам, кончающим школу через месяц.
Поговорите со студентами, кончающими школу через месяц.

blocks.text: The past active participle, like the present active participle, is a verbal adjective; it denotes the performer of an action which took place in the past. It can be formed both from perfective and imperfective verbs: *писавший* = который писал; *написавший* = который написал.

Group 1: verbs ending in **-л** in the past tense. The participle is formed from the past tense (masculine) by dropping **-л** and adding the suffix **-вш-** before the adjectival ending: **проверял** — **проверявший**; **проверил** — **проверивший**. From **-ся** verbs, **-ся** (never **-сь**) is added after the adjectival ending: **мылся** — **мывшийся**.

Group 2: verbs ending in the past tense (masc.) in any other consonant but **-л** add the suffix **-ш-** + adjectival ending: **принёс** — **принёсший**; **погиб** — **погибший**; **спасся** — **спасшийся**. Exception: **исчезнуть** — **исчез** — **исчезнувший**.

Group 3: the verb **идти** with its derivatives and some verbs in **-сти** change the **-л** of the past tense to **д** or **т** (appearing in the present stem) before **-ший**: **идти** (**иду**) — **шедший**; **вести** (**веду**) — **ведший**; **изобрести** (**изобрету**) — **изобретший**. The same in derivatives: **прийти** — **пришедший**; **перевести** — **переведший**.
The stress coincides with that of the past tense (masculine).

Past active participles: 1) do not have short forms; 2) are used only as modifiers, agreeing in gender, number and case with the word modified; 3) are declined like adjectives; 4) when used alone always precede the word modified; 5) can form participial phrases which may be located before or after the word modified.

items: На упавшем самолёте летел мой начальник.
Лётчик, прилетевший вчера из Арктики, привёз важные сведения.

blocks.text: Participial phrases can be replaced by «**который**» clauses, in which «**который**» is a subject and the verb is in the past tense: *Генерал наградил лётчика, сбившего два самолёта = который сбил два самолёта. В вагонах сидели солдаты, возвращавшиеся с фронта = которые возвращались с фронта.* Sometimes the present active participle is used instead, to emphasize simultaneous action: *Вчера мы видели горящий дом.*

The numerals **оба** and **обе** are declined like soft adjectives in the plural: **обоих** (**братьев**), **обеих** (**сестёр**), **обоим**, **обеим**, **обоими**, **обеими**, **об обоих**, **об обеих**. They agree with the nouns like **два** — **две**: *Мы видели оба трактора и обоих шофёров. Передайте эти книги обоим учителям и обеим учительницам.*
Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Какая у тебя была ___ (профилировать) дисциплина в университете?
exercises.prompt: What did you major in at college?
exercises.why: **профилировать → профилирующая** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: The war lasting for years impoverished the country.
exercises.why: **длиться → длившаяся** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Stop being so judgmental.
exercises.why: **осуждать → осуждающим** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: The dodo is an extinct animal.
exercises.why: **вымереть → вымершее** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: The dam blocking the river is very wide.
exercises.why: **перегораживать → Перегораживающая** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.q: Я нашёл ___ (проржаветь) нож с серебряной рукоятью.
exercises.prompt: I found a rusty knife with a silver handle.
exercises.why: **проржаветь → проржавевший** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.q: Вам следует принять соответствующие меры в ___ (соответствовать) время.
exercises.prompt: You should take the appropriate measures at the appropriate time.
exercises.why: **соответствовать → соответствующее** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Tom was wet and cold.
exercises.why: **промокнуть → промокший** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Tom has split ends.
exercises.why: **сечься → секущиеся** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.q: Даниил был первым офицером, ___ (прибыть) на место преступления.
exercises.prompt: Dan was the first officer to arrive at the crime scene.
exercises.why: **прибыть → прибывшим** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: The lights emit a faint buzzing sound.
exercises.why: **жужжать → жужжащий** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Tom is a chess grandmaster.
exercises.why: **получить → получивший** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: The word "laborer" is a noun derived from the word "labor".
exercises.why: **происходить → происходящее** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.q: ___ (войти) в нашу комнату кошка испуганно озиралась.
exercises.prompt: The cat that entered our room looked around, frightened.
exercises.why: **войти → Вошедшая** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Snakes are reptiles.
exercises.why: **пресмыкаться → пресмыкающиеся** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: He has a unibrow.
exercises.why: **срастись → сросшиеся** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.q: Она стала ___ (заведовать) отделением кардиологии в городской больнице.
exercises.prompt: She became the director of the cardiology department at the city hospital.
exercises.why: **заведовать → заведующей** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Is it OK to eat moldy bread?
exercises.why: **заплесневеть → заплесневевший** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.

exercises.q: Он невольно поморщился от боли, ___ (пульсировать) в спине.
exercises.prompt: Despite himself, he winced at the pain that throbbed in his back.
exercises.why: **пульсировать → пульсирующей** — present active participle: 3rd person plural without -т + -щ- + adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: She cherished the memory of her dead husband.
exercises.why: **уйти → ушедшем** — past active participle: past stem + -вш- (after a vowel) or -ш- (after a consonant) + adjective ending.
